sentences.text:
2.  The first bail application of the applicant was heard and disposed of by this Court vide order dated 16.10.2024.
3.

Learned counsel for the applicant contends that the allegations regarding the applicant sending objectionable videos to the nephew of the informant and threatening to make the same viral on Instagram and Facebook are false and baseless.
It is urged that there is no evidence on record to substantiate these allegations and, therefore, no offence under Section 67 of the I.T. Act is made out.
It is further submitted that there is no medical evidence supporting the allegations of rape.
The applicant has been in judicial custody since 09.07.2024 and has no previous criminal history.

4. Learned A.G.A., opposing the prayer for bail, submits that this being the second bail application,
the applicant has not disclosed any fresh ground warranting reconsideration.

It is pointed out that the mobile phone allegedly used in the commission of the offence was sent for FSL examination, and the report indicates that the device, being an iPhone, was digitally locked and could not be connected to the server; consequently, data could not be retrieved.
It is further submitted that the grounds presently raised were already considered and rejected by this Court at the time of the first bail application.
In the absence of any substantial change in circumstances, it is contended that a subsequent bail application is not maintainable.
Reliance is placed on the settled principle that successive bail applications may be entertained only upon the emergence of new facts or changed circumstances having a material bearing on the case.

5. Upon consideration of the rival submissions and perusal of the record, it is evident that the applicant?s first bail application was rejected by this Court after due consideration of all relevant materials.
The present application does not disclose any fresh ground or change in circumstance subsequent to that rejection.

The contentions advanced by learned counsel for the applicant,
touching upon the appreciation of evidence or credibility of witnesses, pertain to matters within the domain of trial and cannot be adjudicated at this stage.
6.

Considering the nature and gravity of the allegations, particularly those involving the offence of rape of a minor girl, and the absence of any new or substantial ground, this Court is not inclined to grant bail to the applicant.

7. In view of the gravity of the offence, the absence of any fresh ground, and the settled legal position Savej vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31778183/
2 governing successive bail applications
